sam: Heads-up — after merging the new checkpoint onboarding (PR #4523) we saw a p99 latency surge on the serving fleet for several models. Noticed immediately in SLO alerts at ~08:34 UTC. Anybody else seeing this?

lee: Yep, I got the alert too. +1 on p99 spike. Affected routes look like small-chat and summarize-heavy. No obvious CPU/GPU saturation on the dashboards.

perf-ci: [CI] buildkite/redwood/inference/serving: perf-regression detected on integration-run 202 (compare: baseline 185 -> current 231 ms p99). See logs: https://ci.internal/bk/202

maria: Quick profiling on a repro node — attaching flame output snippet. Looks like KV cache hit rate dropped ~12% and there's extra memcpy activity during tokenization path. Suspect tokenizer change in checkpoint metadata + kernel fallback for short sequences.

maria: ```
# top hotspots (sampled)
0. memcpy (user)                 28.3%
1. tokenizer::normalize           14.7%
2. kv_cache::evict_hotloop         9.8%
3. kernel_selector::fallback       8.9%
```

arjun: Interesting — the new tokenizer pads differently (leading space preservation) which changes sequence boundaries sent to runtime. That can break prefix KV cache indexing and force more cache misses + rekeying. Also we recently changed kernel selection threshold for short sequences in 7f3b2ad (auto-fallback enabled). Might be an interaction.

sam: Can we bisect to narrow to checkpoint vs kernel-selection change? I can revert either but want confidence.

lee: I ran a quick bisect across merges between last-green and head. The bisect points at a merge that updates checkpoint metadata + tokenizer mapping: commit 7f9c4e2. When I force the old tokenizer mapping the repro p99 drops back ~18ms.

maria: Reproduced locally: toggling kernel_selector.short_seq_threshold = 8 -> 12 also changes behavior. When threshold is lower we stay on the optimized kernel and p99 improves. With new tokenizer the seq length distribution shifted by +1 token frequently, pushing some requests into fallback path.

jen: We should do a hotfix revert of the checkpoint metadata while we investigate. I'll prepare revert PR.

perf-ci: [CI] perf-run for revert-pr #4531 queued.

jen: Revert PR opened and flagged as rollout-blocker. cc @deploy-bot for expedited deploy.

deploy-bot: Starting canary deploy for revert-pr #4531 -> staging. 4/5 canaries healthy.

lee: After canary traffic routed, staging p99 back at baseline. Canary metrics look good, rolling to prod now.

deploy-bot: Rollout to prod complete. All checks passed.

sam: Nice work. Next steps: (1) add a synthetic eval that measures tokenizer-induced seq-length shift for new checkpoints, (2) add a KV cache unit test that simulates leading-space-preserving tokenization, (3) revisit kernel-selection heuristics to be robust to +1 token shifts.

arjun: I can own (3) — will draft a change that makes selection hysteretic (only switch kernels if sustained across N requests) so small tokenizer deltas won't flip the kernel and cause p99 regressions.

maria: I'll add the eval and a short repro script. For the record: here's the quick repro command I used:
```bash
# repro (short chat workload)
python infra/repro/run_inference.py --model redwood-checkpoint-2026-03 --prompt-file tests/data/short_chat.txt --traces kv,profile --warmup 50 --iter 200
```

jen: Keeping the revert PR in place until we ship the kernel-selection hysteresis + tokenizer test in a follow-up. Marking rollout-blocker resolved but flagged for postmortem.

sam: Thanks everyone. Filing a short incident note and linking bisect/PRs. We'll follow up in the postmortem with concrete threshold numbers and test coverage. :thumbsup:
